$comment: Registry of landing sections. Agents read this file to learn what is available instead of guessing from the code. The sequence in 'order' is the valid order on a page.

visuals.terminal: A command-line block. lines[]: { text, tone?: 'dim'|'ok' }. Use it to prove a technical claim with real output.
visuals.stats: A grid of 4 figures. items[]: { value, label }. Use it when you have concrete numbers.
visuals.image: A full-bleed image with no radius. { src, alt }. Use it when you have a real product photograph.

nav.use: Always present, first on the page.

props.links: {label,href}[] (3–5, or [] when the page has no menu)
props.cta: {label,href}? (omit when the page has no action in the header)

hero.use: Always present, straight after the nav. The product promise.

manifesto.use: A single statement sentence. Drop it on short pages.

split.use: Explains how it works. Drop it on short pages.

feature.use: One dark block per main feature. Repeat 1–3 times, alternating visualSide.

testimonial.use: Social proof. single: one large quote. pair: two smaller quotes. Both may appear, with single first.

cta.use: Present by default, before the footer. Verb plus outcome within a time frame. Drop it only when the page deliberately has no action — then the footer is the only way out.

footer.use: Always present, at the end of the page.

props.place: string? (place name at the right of the meta line, defaults to 'Portland')

comparison.use: An honest comparison with the old way. Drop it when there is nothing to compare.

pricing.use: A price table of 2–4 tiers, exactly one featured (inverted ink).

timeline.use: Milestones in chronological order: a project schedule by week, or a company history. Drop it on short pages.

props.title: string
props.items: {marker,label,text}[] (3–6). marker is a real point in time (week/month/year), label ≤ 6 words, text ≤ 30 words.

team.use: A photo of people actually working plus one verifiable commitment. Place it after testimonial, before the CTA. Drop it when there is no real photo.

placeholders: Missing a real figure, name, or quote → write '[real number needed]' / '[real name needed]' in its place. Never invent one.
